nodes.label: Blues
nodes.summary: A root system for much of modern guitar music, built around call and response, bent notes, shuffle feel and personal storytelling.

nodes.label: Electric blues
nodes.summary: Blues amplified for clubs, cities and louder bands. It shaped rock guitar tone, soloing and the idea of the electric guitar as a lead voice.

nodes.label: Rock and roll
nodes.summary: A high-energy meeting point between blues, country, gospel and rhythm and blues, with the guitar pushed toward the front.

nodes.label: Rock
nodes.summary: The broad guitar-centered field that branches into psychedelic rock, progressive rock, hard rock, metal, punk and grunge.

nodes.label: Psychedelic rock
nodes.summary: A late-1960s rock branch marked by effects, improvisation, studio experimentation and expanded guitar textures.

nodes.label: Progressive rock
nodes.summary: Rock music stretched toward longer forms, concept albums, unusual harmony and more cinematic guitar arrangements.

nodes.label: Hard rock
nodes.summary: Louder blues-rock DNA with heavier riffs, thicker amps and an arena-sized guitar sound.

nodes.label: Heavy metal
nodes.summary: A heavier guitar tradition built around riffs, distortion, volume and darker harmonic colors.

nodes.label: Punk rock
nodes.summary: Direct, sharp and often minimal guitar music that reacted against excess and pushed attitude to the front.

nodes.label: Grunge
nodes.summary: A rough-edged Seattle-centered rock movement where punk urgency met heavy guitar weight and melodic songwriting.

nodes.label: Folk
nodes.summary: Song-centered acoustic traditions where the guitar often works as both rhythm instrument and storytelling companion.

nodes.label: Country
nodes.summary: American roots music with strong acoustic, electric and fingerstyle guitar traditions.

nodes.label: Norwegian vise
nodes.summary: A Nordic song tradition where lyric, humor, melody and acoustic instruments often carry equal weight.

nodes.label: Funk
nodes.summary: Rhythm-first music where guitar often becomes a clipped, syncopated engine inside the groove.

nodes.label: Jazz fusion
nodes.summary: A meeting of jazz harmony, rock volume, funk rhythm and expanded improvisation.

nodes.label: B.B. King
nodes.summary: One of electric blues' defining guitar voices, known for vocal phrasing, controlled vibrato and his Gibson-based Lucille guitars.

nodes.label: Lead Belly
nodes.summary: A major folk and blues figure whose repertoire and twelve-string guitar style fed later folk, blues and rock musicians.

nodes.label: Chuck Berry
nodes.summary: A foundational rock and roll guitarist and songwriter whose riffs, double-stops and showmanship became a rock grammar.

nodes.label: Elvis Presley
nodes.summary: A rock and roll catalyst who helped bring country, blues and rhythm and blues language into mass popular culture.

nodes.label: Jimi Hendrix
nodes.summary: A transformative electric guitarist who expanded feedback, fuzz, wah, chord melody and studio sound into a new rock language.

nodes.label: Stevie Ray Vaughan
nodes.summary: A Texas blues-rock guitarist who revived electric blues guitar for a new generation with huge Stratocaster tone and fierce phrasing.

nodes.label: Eric Clapton
nodes.summary: A blues-rock guitarist linked to the Yardbirds, Cream and a long solo career across electric blues, rock and pop.

nodes.label: David Gilmour
nodes.summary: Pink Floyd's lead guitarist and singer, known for melodic bends, spacious tone and cinematic solo construction.

nodes.label: Mark Knopfler
nodes.summary: Dire Straits' guitarist and songwriter, recognized for clean fingerstyle electric playing and economical melodic phrasing.

nodes.label: Eddie Van Halen
nodes.summary: A technical and sonic innovator whose tapping, harmonics, tremolo work and self-built guitar pushed hard rock guitar forward.

nodes.label: Frank Zappa
nodes.summary: A composer, bandleader and guitarist who connected rock, jazz fusion, satire and complex arrangement.

nodes.label: Johnny Marr
nodes.summary: The Smiths' guitarist, known for layered arpeggios, bright rhythm parts and a melodic alternative-rock vocabulary.

nodes.label: Randy Rhoads
nodes.summary: A neoclassical-leaning metal guitarist whose work with Ozzy Osbourne made precision and classical influence central to heavy guitar.

nodes.label: Tony Iommi
nodes.summary: Black Sabbath's guitarist and a core architect of heavy metal riffing, with dark tuning choices and massive SG-driven tone.

nodes.label: Jimmy Page
nodes.summary: Led Zeppelin's guitarist and producer, central to hard rock through riffs, acoustic textures, studio craft and blues reinvention.

nodes.label: George Harrison
nodes.summary: The Beatles' lead guitarist, whose melodic parts, twelve-string sounds and Indian music interests broadened rock guitar color.

nodes.label: Bob Dylan
nodes.summary: A songwriter who linked folk, blues, rock and electric controversy, reshaping what guitar-led songwriting could carry.

nodes.label: Johnny Cash
nodes.summary: A country figure whose spare rhythm guitar, voice and storytelling style became instantly recognizable.

nodes.label: Willie Nelson
nodes.summary: A country songwriter and guitarist whose nylon-string guitar Trigger became part of his musical identity.

nodes.label: Chet Atkins
nodes.summary: A country guitar master and producer whose fingerstyle approach shaped Nashville guitar vocabulary.

nodes.label: John Mayer
nodes.summary: A modern guitarist and songwriter who draws a clear line from blues guitar vocabulary into pop, soul and jam settings.

nodes.label: Øystein Sunde
nodes.summary: A Norwegian singer-songwriter and guitarist known for fast wordplay, humor, acoustic precision and links to Gitarkameratene.

nodes.label: James Hetfield
nodes.summary: Metallica's rhythm guitarist and vocalist, known for tight downpicking and precise heavy-metal rhythm architecture.

nodes.label: Prince
nodes.summary: A multi-instrumentalist whose guitar work fused funk, rock, pop and soul with theatrical precision and explosive solos.

nodes.label: The Beatles
nodes.summary: A central 1960s band whose songwriting, studio practice and guitar textures reshaped pop and rock music.

nodes.label: Pink Floyd
nodes.summary: A psychedelic and progressive rock band built around atmosphere, albums, sound design and David Gilmour's melodic guitar.

nodes.label: Led Zeppelin
nodes.summary: A hard rock band that fused blues, folk, riffs and studio ambition into a huge guitar-centered sound.

nodes.label: Black Sabbath
nodes.summary: A Birmingham band whose dark riffs, volume and atmosphere became a foundation for heavy metal.

nodes.label: Van Halen

nodes.label: Dire Straits
nodes.summary: A British band centered on Mark Knopfler's clean fingerstyle electric guitar and narrative songwriting.

nodes.label: The Smiths

nodes.label: Ozzy Osbourne

nodes.label: Metallica

nodes.label: Gitarkameratene

nodes.label: Cream

nodes.label: The Yardbirds

nodes.label: Fender

nodes.label: Gibson

nodes.label: C.F. Martin & Co.
nodes.summary: A major acoustic guitar maker whose dreadnought designs are deeply tied to folk, country and singer-songwriter traditions.

nodes.label: Rickenbacker

nodes.label: Gretsch

nodes.label: ESP

nodes.label: Fender Telecaster

nodes.label: Fender Jaguar

nodes.label: ESP Explorer style

nodes.label: Hohner Mad Cat

nodes.label: Banjo

nodes.label: National resonator

nodes.label: Blues rock
nodes.summary: A bridge between electric blues phrasing and louder rock bands, central to late-1960s and 1970s guitar vocabulary.

nodes.label: Rockabilly

nodes.label: Surf rock

nodes.label: Southern rock

nodes.label: Glam rock

nodes.label: Art rock
nodes.summary: Rock music pushed toward art-school experimentation, album-scale ideas and unusual guitar textures.

nodes.label: Alternative rock

nodes.label: Indie rock
nodes.summary: Guitar music shaped by independent scenes, smaller production ideals and melodic or textural experimentation.

nodes.label: Post-punk
nodes.summary: A sharper, exploratory aftermath of punk where guitar could become angular, atmospheric or rhythm-first.

nodes.label: Shoegaze

nodes.label: Thrash metal

nodes.label: Doom metal

nodes.label: Progressive metal

nodes.label: Bluegrass

nodes.label: Singer-songwriter

nodes.label: Jazz
